### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A27, A36, A37, A42 and A43 appear in every trace (participation 100%, up from about 50%) and their mean occurrences per trace rise to about 1.0. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- A02 appears in about 28% of traces (up from 8%) and its mean occurrences rise from 0.09 to 0.29; A10 drops from 12% to 3% participation. [OCC001, OCC002]
- A02's outgoing transitions shift to A15 (about 86% of transitions after, versus none before), and A14's transitions shift partly to A02 (24% after). [DIR001, DIR002]
- A25's successor changes from A28 (98% before) to A43, A42, A37 and A36 (about 28%, 25%, 27% and 18% after). [DIR003]
- A26's successor becomes A27 (98.5% after, versus 45% before). [DIR004]
- A36, A37, A42 and A43 now have A28 as a successor (about 21–28% of transitions) and no longer go to A31. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- Positions: A02, A36, A37, A42 and A43 move earlier (e.g., A36 mean position from 0.58 to 0.41; A02 from 0.51 to 0.19); A26 and A28 move later. [POS001, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS004, POS006]
- A02 now co-occurs with A25, A26, A27, A28, A31, A36, A37, A42 and A43 in about 28% of traces (up from 5–8%), and A02 precedes them in most of those. [REL001–REL009]
- A14, A15 and A25 now co-occur with A27, A36, A37, A42 and A43 in all traces (up from about 50%) and precede them. [REL010–REL024]
- A26 and A28 now follow A36, A37, A42 and A43 (B_before_A ≈ 1.0) instead of preceding them. [REL026–REL029, REL036–REL039]
- Lags: A14 to A02 becomes almost always lag 1 (98% after, versus a spread before); A25 to A28 changes from lag 1 (99%) to lag 5 (99%); A02 to A15 becomes mostly lag 1. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which a group of activities (A27, A36, A37, A42, A43) become mandatory and occur earlier, with a new successor A28, while A31 moves later and A02 becomes more frequent with a new successor A15. The change is directly shown by participation, routing, position and order indicators that agree with each other. The number of qualifying items far exceeds the chance expectation (about 1 item expected, many observed), so the overall pattern is unlikely to be a random split artefact. A competing explanation is that the later window simply contains a different mix of trace variants, but the consistency across indicators and the large number of items make a structural modification the more plausible interpretation. Some individual items rest on few observations (e.g., LAG001 before support 1, LAG006 after support 1), but the main pattern is supported by many well-supported items.
